q.q: What is the main reason computers use binary?
o: Binary numbers use less electricity than denary
Binary was invented specially for computers
Transistors are switches with only two states
Computers can only count up to two
q.why: Each transistor is either on (1) or off (0), so two digits match the hardware.

q.q: What is a transistor?
o: A group of eight binary digits
A device that converts sound to binary
A tiny electronic switch on a chip
A unit used to measure file size
q.why: Processors contain billions of microscopic transistor switches.

q.q: Why are two voltage levels more reliable than ten?
o: Ten levels would need ten times as many cables
It is easy to tell on from off even if the voltage wobbles
Computers cannot measure voltage at all
Two levels make the computer run on batteries
q.why: With only two states, small changes in voltage do not cause errors.

q.q: How many different patterns can 5 bits make?
q.why: 2 to the power 5 is 32. 31 is the largest number, not the number of patterns.

q.q: What is the largest number that can be stored using 4 bits?
q.why: 4 bits give 16 patterns, from 0 to 15.

q.q: A club needs a unique binary code for each of 50 members. What is the smallest number of bits needed?
q.why: 5 bits give 32 patterns (too few); 6 bits give 64.

q.q: What happens to the number of possible patterns each time one bit is added?
q.why: Every old pattern can now end in 0 or 1, so the number doubles.

q.q: A pupil says the pattern 01000001 always means the letter A. Why are they wrong?
o: It means the number 1 in binary
It could also be a number, colour or sound value
Binary patterns never stand for letters
q.why: A bit pattern only has meaning once the computer knows what type of data it represents.

q.q: What are the place values of an 8-bit binary number from left to right?
q.why: Start at 1 on the right and double as you move left.

q.q: In denary, each column is worth how many times the column to its right?
q.why: Denary is base 10, so each column is ten times the one before.

q.q: What is the place value of the fourth bit from the right?
q.why: From the right the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8.

q.q: What is the most significant bit?
o: The left-most bit, with the largest place value
The right-most bit, with a value of 1
Any bit that has the value 1
The bit that is carried in an addition
q.why: In a byte the MSB is worth 128.

q.q: Which binary number must be even?
q.why: Only 10110110 ends in 0, so its 1s column is off.

q.q: What comes straight after 0111 when counting in binary?
q.why: 0111 is 7, so the next number is 8, which is 1000.

q.q: How should the binary number 10 be read aloud?
q.why: In binary, 10 is 2. Saying it digit by digit avoids confusing it with denary ten.

q.q: Which power of 2 is the 64 column?
q.why: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 64. The columns start at 2 to the power 0 = 1.

q.q: What is 00100110 in denary?
What is 10000011 in denary?
What is 110 in denary?
q.why: Lined up on the right it fills the 4 and 2 columns: 4 + 2 = 6.

q.q: What is 01001001 in denary?
What is 11100000 in denary?
Without fully converting it, what can you say about 10000110?
o: It is odd and at least 128
It is even and less than 128
It is even and at least 128
It is odd and less than 128
q.why: The MSB is 1 so it is 128 or more, and the last bit is 0 so it is even.

q.q: Ryan converts 00000101 and gets 160. What mistake did he make?
o: He added the 0 columns instead of the 1s
He forgot to add the 1s column
He read the place values from the left
q.why: 128 + 32 = 160 uses the wrong end. The right answer is 4 + 1 = 5.

q.q: Which binary number is the same as denary 100?
What is denary 42 in 8-bit binary?
What is denary 255 in 8-bit binary?
q.why: 255 is the total of every place value in a byte.

q.q: What is denary 9 in 8-bit binary?
q.why: 8 + 1 = 9, so only the 8 and 1 columns are on.

q.q: When converting 150 with the subtraction method, what is left after taking away 128?
q.why: 150 - 128 = 22, so move on to the 64 column with 22 left.

q.q: What is denary 220 in 8-bit binary?
Why is 1101 not a full answer when asked for 13 as an 8-bit number?
o: It needs leading zeros to make 8 bits
q.why: The correct 8-bit answer is 00001101.

q.q: Using the dividing by 2 method on 6, the remainders are 0, 1, 1. What is 6 in binary?
q.why: Read the remainders from the bottom up: 110 = 4 + 2 = 6.

q.q: What is the smallest denary number that cannot be stored in 8 bits?
q.why: 8 bits store 0 to 255, so 256 needs a ninth bit.

q.q: In binary addition, what do you write and carry for 1 + 1?
q.why: 1 + 1 = 2 = 10 in binary.

q.q: In binary addition, what do you write and carry for 1 + 1 + 1?
q.why: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 = 11 in binary.

q.q: What is an overflow error?
o: A result needs more bits than are available
A file is too big for the storage device
A program runs for too long
A carry is added to the 1s column
q.why: The extra bit is lost, so the stored answer is wrong.

q.q: Which 8-bit addition would cause an overflow?
q.why: 240 + 32 = 272, which is more than 255. The others give 254, 255 and 255.

q.q: 200 + 100 is calculated in an 8-bit register and only the right-most 8 bits are kept. What value is stored?
q.why: 300 is 100101100; dropping the ninth bit leaves 00101100 = 44.

q.q: What is the best way to check a binary addition?
o: Add the numbers again from left to right
Count how many 1s are in the answer
Check that the answer has 8 bits
Convert both numbers and the answer to denary
q.why: If the denary sum matches the denary answer, the binary sum is right.

q.q: Why can an overflow cause bugs that are hard to spot?
o: The computer always crashes straight away
The answer is rounded to the nearest 10
The computer asks the user to fix it
The computer may carry on with a wrong answer and no warning
q.why: Unless a program checks for overflow, the wrong value is used silently.

q.q: How many bytes are in 1 kilobyte, as used in CCEA questions?
q.why: CCEA uses 1 KB = 1024 bytes, because 1024 is 2 to the power 10.

q.q: Which unit is 1024 megabytes?
q.why: KB, MB, GB, TB: each is 1024 of the one before.

q.q: How many bits are in 3 KB?
How many MB is 2,048 KB?
q.why: Smaller to bigger unit: divide. 2,048 / 1024 = 2.

q.q: How many 256 MB files fit on an 8 GB memory card?
Niamh divides 64 GB by 4 MB and gets 16 photos. What went wrong?
o: She should have multiplied instead of dividing
She should have used 1000 instead of 1024
She did not change both sizes to the same unit first
She should have divided by 8 for bits

q.q: Which pair of features most affects a computer's performance?
o: Case colour and number of USB ports
q.why: More RAM and a faster processor let the computer do more, more quickly.

q.q: What does a clock speed of 3 GHz mean?
q.why: Giga means billion and hertz means per second.

q.q: How many different digits does hexadecimal use?
q.why: 0 to 9 plus A to F makes 16 digits.

q.q: What is hex F in denary?
How many bits does one hex digit represent?
q.why: One hex digit is exactly one nibble.

q.q: What is 10011110 in hexadecimal?
What is hex 4C in denary?
What is denary 255 in hexadecimal?
What is hex A7 in 8-bit binary?
In the web colour #FF0000, what do the first two hex digits control?
q.why: Colours are written as RRGGBB, so the first pair is red.

q.q: Which is the best reason programmers use hexadecimal?
o: The computer stores data in hexadecimal
It uses less storage space than binary
It is shorter and easier to read than binary
It can only be read by programmers
q.why: Hex is a shorthand for people; the computer still stores binary.

q.q: What does ASCII stand for?
o: American System for Computer Information Input
American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Automatic Standard Code for Internet Information
Advanced System Code for Information Interchange
q.why: ASCII is a character set first published in the 1960s.

q.q: How many characters can standard 7-bit ASCII represent?
q.why: 2 to the power 7 is 128 different codes.

q.q: In ASCII, A = 65. What is the code for M?
q.why: M is the 13th letter: 64 + 13 = 77. 109 is lower case m.

q.q: What is the ASCII code for the space character?
q.why: A space is a character too, with code 32.

q.q: The ASCII code for b is 98. What is the code for B?
q.why: Capitals are 32 less than lower case: 98 - 32 = 66.

q.q: Decode the ASCII codes 79 75.
How many bits are needed to store the text Erne Bridge in ASCII, at one byte per character?
q.why: E-r-n-e is 4, the space is 1 and B-r-i-d-g-e is 6: 11 characters x 8 bits = 88.

q.q: Why was Unicode developed?
o: To make English text files smaller
To include characters from all languages and emoji
q.why: ASCII has only 128 codes, enough for English but not for other writing systems.

q.q: Which data type stores only True or False?
q.why: A Boolean has just two values.

q.q: Which data type is best for a pupil's height of 1.58 m?
q.why: The value has a decimal part.

q.q: Which data type is best for the number of tickets sold?
q.why: You cannot sell half a ticket, so a whole number is right.

q.q: How is the string "Hi" stored in ASCII?
o: As the codes 72 and 105, one byte each
q.why: A string is stored as one character code after another.

q.q: What is the minimum storage a Boolean value needs?
q.why: Two values, so one bit (1 = True, 0 = False) is enough.

q.q: Which data type should be used for a postcode such as BT74 6AA?
q.why: It contains letters, digits and a space.

q.q: How is the integer 6 stored differently from the string "6"?
o: As 00000110 rather than the character code 54
As a float rather than a Boolean
q.why: The integer is the binary number 6; the character 6 has ASCII code 54 (00110110).

q.q: What does "3" + "4" give when both values are strings?
q.why: Adding strings joins them together (concatenation).

q.q: Which statement about floats is true?
o: They can only store whole numbers
They always use exactly one byte
Some decimals, like 0.1, cannot be stored exactly
They are stored as character codes
q.why: Floats store digits plus a power, and some fractions never end in binary.

q.q: What is a pixel?
o: The number of bits used for each colour
The smallest single point of colour in an image
A group of 8 bits in an image file
The width of an image in centimetres
q.why: Pixel is short for picture element.

q.q: What is colour depth?
o: The number of pixels across an image
The number of bits used for each pixel
The number of colours in a palette file
q.why: n bits per pixel gives 2 to the power n colours.

q.q: How many colours can a colour depth of 3 bits give?
q.why: 2 to the power 3 = 8.

q.q: An image has 1024 x 768 pixels. What is this called?
q.why: Resolution is width x height in pixels.

q.q: What is the file size of a 16 x 16 icon with a colour depth of 4 bits?
A 100 x 50 image uses 16 colours. What is its size in bits?
q.why: 16 colours need 4 bits: 100 x 50 x 4 = 20,000 bits.

q.q: What happens to the file size if the colour depth goes from 8 bits to 24 bits?
q.why: Each pixel now needs 24 bits instead of 8: 24 / 8 = 3.

q.q: Why does a small photo look blocky when printed on a large poster?
o: Each pixel is enlarged, causing pixelation
The printer changes the colour depth
The file gains extra pixels when printed
q.why: No new detail is added, so the pixels show as squares.

q.q: Why does an image file also store metadata such as its width?
o: So the image can be compressed with RLE
To increase the colour depth of the image
So the computer knows where each row of pixels ends
To make the file size smaller
q.why: The pixel codes are stored in one long list, so the width is needed to rebuild the grid.

q.q: Why must sound be sampled before a computer can store it?
o: Sound is analogue but computers store digital data
Sound is too fast for a computer to hear
q.why: Sampling turns the continuous wave into binary numbers.

q.q: What is the sample rate measured in?
q.why: Hertz means samples per second.

q.q: What is the sample rate of CD-quality audio?
q.why: CDs take 44,100 samples per second with 16-bit samples.

q.q: What does bit depth mean for sound?
o: The number of samples taken each second
The number of bits used to store each sample
The length of the recording in seconds
q.why: Higher bit depth means more levels, so each sample is more precise.

q.q: A 10-second mono clip uses a sample rate of 8,000 Hz and 8-bit samples. What is its size in bytes?
What is the bit rate of a mono recording at 22,050 Hz with 16-bit samples?
q.why: Bit rate = sample rate x bit depth = 22,050 x 16 = 352,800.

q.q: What effect does a higher sample rate have?
o: Better quality and a smaller file
Worse quality and a larger file
No change to quality or file size
Better quality and a larger file
q.why: More samples capture the wave better, but there is more data to store.

q.q: A pupil calculates a 2-minute stereo clip using 2 for the length and 1 for the channels. Which two errors have they made?
o: Length should be 2 hours and channels 1
Length should be 120 seconds and channels 1
Length should be 60 seconds and channels 4
Length should be 120 seconds and channels 2
q.why: Minutes must become seconds (x 60) and stereo has 2 channels.

q.q: Which is a reason for compressing files?
o: They take less time to send over the internet
They can be read without software
q.why: Smaller files transfer faster and use less storage.

q.q: What does lossy compression do?
o: Permanently removes some data to make a much smaller file
Keeps every bit so the original can be rebuilt
Makes the file bigger to improve quality
Changes the file into plain text
q.why: Lost data can never be recovered.

q.q: Which group of formats all use lossless compression?
q.why: jpeg, mp3 and mp4 are lossy.

q.q: What is WWWWWWWWBB in run-length encoding?
q.why: 8 white pixels then 2 black pixels.

q.q: Which type of compression should be used for a computer program file?
o: Lossy, because it makes the smallest file
Lossless, because every bit is needed
Lossy, because programs are mostly text
Neither, as programs cannot be compressed
q.why: Losing even one bit could stop the program working.

q.q: Why does RLE work badly on a detailed photograph?
o: There are few long runs of the same colour
Photographs are always stored as text
RLE only works on sound files
q.why: With few repeats, writing a count before each value can even make the file bigger.

q.q: A wav song is 30 MB. The same song as an mp3 is about 11 times smaller. Roughly how big is the mp3?
q.why: 30 / 11 is about 2.7 MB.

q.q: Why would a photographer keep an uncompressed original rather than re-saving a jpeg many times?
o: jpeg files can only be opened once
Re-saving changes the resolution to 1 x 1
Each lossy save removes a little more detail
q.why: Lossy compression throws away data each time it is applied.
